routes.label: Prove divisibility and then prove maximality

solution:
Because \(n\) is even, the five factors are consecutive odd integers. Odd multiples of \(3\) occur every third odd number, so the first three factors include a multiple of \(3\). Odd multiples of \(5\) occur every fifth odd number, so the five factors include a multiple of \(5\). Thus every allowed product is divisible by \(15\).

To prove that \(15\) is the largest universal divisor, it is enough to find two allowed products whose greatest common factor is \(15\). Let \(P(n)\) denote the given product. Taking \(n=10\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(10)&=11\cdot13\cdot15\cdot17\cdot19\\
&=3\cdot5\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking \(n=20\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(20)&=21\cdot23\cdot25\cdot27\cdot29\\
&=3^4\cdot5^2\cdot7\cdot23\cdot29.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their only shared prime factors are \(3\) and \(5\), each appearing just once in \(P(10)\), so their greatest common factor is \(15\). Any integer dividing every allowed product must divide these two products and hence must divide \(15\).

Since \(15\) always works and no larger integer can work, the answer is \(\boxed{15}\), choice \(\text{D}\).
